articles.title: How to watch Sixers vs. Bulls on Nov. 2: Game preview, line ups, injury reports and more
articles.summary: The 6-1 Philadelphia 76ers host the Chicago Bulls on Monday night at Xfinity Mobile Arena, with tip-off set for 7:30 p.m. EST. It is a short stay at home.
articles.body: The 6-1 Philadelphia 76ers host the Chicago Bulls on Monday night at Xfinity Mobile Arena, with tip-off set for 7:30 p.m. EST. It is a short stay at home. The Sixers fly to Detroit on Wednesday to open a three-game road trip that also stops in Cleveland and Chicago. Jaylen Brown, the veteran forward who missed Friday’s win over the New York Knicks, was left off the weekend injury report and looks set to start. Joel Embiid is listed as questionable with right foot plantar fascia injury management. Dominick Barlow and Ariel Hukporti are out. Chicago may be without Nic Claxton, who is doubtful. Here is where to watch, who is hurt and who is expected to start.Sixers vs. Bulls: Game previewPhiladelphia’s 6-1 start has included some rallies. The Sixers have won games from behind, and they would rather stop needing to. The aim against Chicago is one clean game over all 48 minutes. The schedule adds some push, since three straight road games follow, at Detroit, Cleveland and Chicago, before the team gets back to Philadelphia.Jaylen Brown’s knee is the main thing to watch. A left patellar tendinopathy sidelined the veteran forward for Friday’s win over the Knicks, his first missed game of the season. Brown returned on Halloween and played 38 minutes in a 109-104 win over Charlotte. The numbers were modest: 16 points, four assists and four rebounds on 40.0% shooting. All four sat below the averages from the first five games, when the forward put up 20.6 points, 6.6 rebounds and 4.2 assists in 36.4 minutes a night, shooting 44.2% overall and 40.9% from three.The same knee trouble showed up earlier in Brown’s career with the Celtics. Coach Nick Nurse suggested the latest setback is not a long-term concern, and Philadelphia left Brown off its first injury report for this game. Barring a change, he starts.Chicago’s projected group has Josh Giddey and Norman Powell in the backcourt, Caleb Wilson and Matas Buzelis up front, and Jalen Smith at center.How to watch Sixers vs. Bulls game on Monday?The game is on NBC Sports Philadelphia, with tip-off at 7:30 p.m. EST. Philadelphia wears its blue Icon Edition uniforms. Chicago is in the red Icon Edition set.Two things are worth watching early. Embiid’s status is the first, and it is the one to check closest to tip-off. The second is how the Sixers start. A fast first quarter would be a change from the games they have had to rescue.Sixers vs. Bulls: date, time, and venueDate: Monday, Nov. 2Time: 7:30 p.m. ESTVenue: Xfinity Mobile Arena, Philadelphia, PATV channel: NBC Sports PhiladelphiaSixers vs. Bulls: Injury ReportPhiladelphia 76ersOut: Dominick Barlow (low back stress reaction)Out: Ariel Hukporti (right Achilles tear)Questionable: Joel Embiid (right foot plantar fascia injury management)Brown is not listed after coming back against the Hornets.Chicago BullsDoubtful: Nic Claxton (left hamstring strain)Probable: Jalen Smith (left finger sprain)Probable: Tobe Awaka (left ankle sprain)Claxton’s doubtful tag makes Smith’s availability matter more. Smith is the projected starting center, finger sprain and all.Sixers vs. Bulls: Probable starting lineupsPhiladelphia 76ersGuard: Tyrese MaxeyGuard: VJ EdgecombeForward: Jaylen BrownForward: LeBron JamesCenter: Joel EmbiidChicago BullsGuard: Josh GiddeyGuard: Norman PowellForward: Caleb WilsonForward: Matas BuzelisCenter: Jalen SmithThese lineups are probable and may change before tip-off, especially with Embiid questionable.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Stephen Curry’s rise to NBA’s highest-paid player was about more than three-pointers, as his career choices and endorsement strategy helped build a $203.6 million fortune
articles.summary: Stephen Curry has agreed to a two-year, $116 million extension with the Golden State Warriors, running through the 2028-29 season.
articles.body: Stephen Curry has agreed to a two-year, $116 million extension with the Golden State Warriors, running through the 2028-29 season. The final year is a player option, a route to a 20th season with the same franchise. Curry was eligible for up to $136 million, so the new deal sits about $20 million below the ceiling. Even with the discount, Curry still tops the 2026-27 salary list at $62.6 million. The numbers point to a career built on more than his three-pointers. A run of contracts, a shoe-brand split and a new apparel deal explain how Curry got here.How did Stephen Curry become the NBA’s highest-paid player?Stephen Curry sits first on the 2026-27 contract list at $62.6 million, ahead of Nikola Jokic at $59 million and Jayson Tatum at $58.5 million. Three contracts and one shaky ankle explain most of the climb.Golden State drafted Curry seventh in 2009. Ankle trouble followed, and by 2012 the Warriors had to decide how much to trust the ankle. They offered a four-year, $44 million extension. It became one of the better bargains in league history. Curry won back-to-back MVP awards and the first two of four titles while playing under it.The large numbers arrived next. In July 2017, Curry signed a five-year, $201.2 million deal, the first in NBA history above $200 million. The contract also made Curry the league’s highest-paid player. In August 2021, a four-year, $215 million extension made Curry the first player with two contracts over $200 million. Yearly pay on that one rose from $48.1 million in 2022-23 to $59.6 million in 2025-26. A one-year, $62.6 million extension signed in August 2024 then covered 2026-27.The September deal works differently. Curry was eligible for $136 million and signed for $116 million. Pay drops to $55.7 million in 2027-28 and $60.2 million in 2028-29, with the second year a player option. Golden State general manager Mike Dunleavy said there has never been “a better face to a franchise in professional sports history.”The $62.6 million guard gave the team breathing room too. A smaller number cuts the Warriors’ future payroll commitment, and it fits a long-held plan to finish a career in one uniform. The agreement arrives after a year in which a right knee injury held Curry to 43 games, though he still averaged 26.6 points.How much has Curry earned from contracts and endorsements?Through the 2025-26 season, Curry had collected $470.1 million in NBA salary. Add $62.6 million for 2026-27 and the $116 million extension, and the projected total reaches $648.7 million, provided the final-year option is picked up. Endorsements, investments and other off-court income sit outside that figure.Shoes carry the other big number. Curry began in Nike gear, then signed with Under Armour in 2013. The partnership grew into Curry Brand in 2020, with Curry serving as its president. A 2023 extension was supposed to run past the end of Curry’s playing days. Instead, the relationship ended in November 2025 and Curry Brand went independent. Under Armour kept releasing previously developed Curry products through 2026 while the brand looked at new partners.In June 2026, Curry signed a 10-year agreement with Chinese sportswear company Li-Ning worth more than $400 million, an average of more than $40 million a year. The deal covers signature shoes, basketball apparel, lifestyle products, and golf, with plans for Curry Brand stores in China and the United States. Curry can also sign other athletes under the brand.What else is in Curry’s business portfolio?Beyond sneakers, Curry has endorsement ties with Fanatics, Google, JPMorgan Chase, Panini, Rakuten and 2K Sports. The wider business interests sit under a company called Thirty Ink, covering media, branding, investments and philanthropy.Unanimous Media, co-founded with Erick Peyton in 2018, develops film, television, documentary, publishing and podcast projects with a lean toward sports, family and faith. Curry starred in the 2024 Peacock comedy “Mr. Throwback” and published the photo book “Shot Ready” in 2025. Other ventures include Gentleman’s Cut bourbon and Underrated, a platform that gives overlooked young athletes basketball and golf programs with competition, development and exposure. Estimates put Curry’s net worth at $350 million.What are Curry’s biggest career accomplishments?Curry is a four-time champion, winning in 2015, 2017, 2018 and 2022, and the 2022 Finals MVP. Curry has two MVP awards, and the 2016 vote is the only unanimous one in league history. In 2015-16, Curry averaged 30.1 points, made 402 three-pointers and led Golden State to an NBA-record 73 wins. The same season produced a 50-40-90 shooting year at more than 30 points a game, something no other player has done.The list keeps going. Curry has 12 All-Star selections, 11 All-NBA nods, and two scoring titles, in 2016 and 2021. Eight seasons ended with Curry leading the league in made threes. In March 2025, Curry became the first player to hit 4,000 career threes. Internationally, Curry owns gold from the 2010 and 2014 FIBA World Cups and the 2024 Paris Olympics, where late threes helped beat France in the final.Inside the Warriors’ record book, Curry holds the most All-Star selections (12) and the most All-NBA selections (11) in franchise history.As for Curry’s NBA career, he is one of the greatest to play the sport, with several stunning records and titles to his name. Many argue that Steph should be in the Greatest of All Time (GOAT) debate alongside Chicago Bulls legend Michael Jordan and, of course, LeBron James. Certainly, he deserves the place. Recently, the NBA’s official social media handle posted a short video asking league-wide stars for their opinion on one great NBA skill one would steal. Many called it Curry’s shooting, and some wanted his ball-handling as well. Regardless, Curry is a forged player; he developed into one of the greatest in the game.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Stephen Curry’s projected $203.6M fortune puts LeBron James’ $93.9M earnings in the shade after his $3.9M 76ers decision
articles.summary: Stephen Curry is heading towards a financial milestone that could put him in a league of his own.
articles.body: Stephen Curry is heading towards a financial milestone that could put him in a league of his own. The Golden State Warriors superstar is projected to earn an astonishing $203.6 million over the coming year, creating a huge gap between him and some of basketball's biggest names. LeBron James remains a commercial powerhouse, but his decision to accept a veteran-minimum contract with the Philadelphia 76ers has changed the financial picture. The difference highlights how Curry has turned his success on the court into an enormous business empire.Stephen Curry’s $203.6 million earnings leave LeBron James trailingCurry has secured the top position on Forbes' 2026 list of the NBA's highest-paid players for a second consecutive year. His projected earnings include $62.6 million from basketball and another $141 million from endorsements and business ventures.The off-court figure is particularly striking. It represents a significant increase from the estimated $100 million he generated through commercial activities the previous year.One of the biggest developments behind Curry's growing business portfolio is his partnership with Chinese sportswear company Li-Ning. After ending his relationship with Under Armour in 2025, the Warriors guard agreed to a 10-year deal worth $400 million.The agreement includes a signature footwear collection expected to launch early next year. It gives Curry another major platform to build his brand beyond the NBA.According to Forbes, Curry is the first active NBA player projected to cross $200 million in earnings over a 12-month period. Only Floyd Mayweather, Cristiano Ronaldo and Jon Rahm have previously reached that mark among athletes tracked by the publication.LeBron James’ $3.9 million 76ers contract changes NBA earnings raceJames has slipped to fourth place on the list after spending 11 consecutive seasons at the top of NBA earnings rankings.His projected income stands at $93.9 million, including approximately $90 million from endorsements and business interests. However, his latest contract decision has reduced his basketball earnings considerably.The 76ers signed the veteran superstar to a minimum deal worth approximately $3.9 million. That decision puts his projected total at less than half of Curry's expected earnings.Kevin Durant occupies second place with $104.9 million, while Giannis Antetokounmpo follows at $103.5 million. Anthony Edwards and Jayson Tatum round out the top six with $87.9 million and $86.5 million, respectively.The wider numbers reveal just how valuable NBA stars have become outside basketball. The ten highest-paid players are projected to generate a combined $958 million, with $469 million coming from endorsements and commercial ventures.For Curry, the achievement goes beyond his basketball salary. At 38, he has built a business portfolio that continues to grow even as the competition for NBA earnings intensifies. James remains one of the sport's biggest commercial names, but Curry currently holds the financial advantage.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: “That would be a giant mistake”: Luka Doncic gets fresh insider warning amid standout season as Los Angeles Lakers’ trade scenario on the horizon
articles.summary: Los Angeles Lakers insider Jovan Buha puts the odds of a trade this season at 65%, and he has a pointed message for the front office.
articles.body: Los Angeles Lakers insider Jovan Buha puts the odds of a trade this season at 65%, and he has a pointed message for the front office. Luka Doncic leads the league in scoring at 38.3 points per game, and the Lakers are 6-2.Buha says sitting still while this is happening would be a costly mistake. Injuries have thinned out the Western Conference, and the roster still has two clear gaps. A deal is unlikely this month. Late December or the February deadline fits better.Is it a mistake for the Lakers to skip a Luka Doncic trade?Buha thinks so. On his podcast, Buha’s Block, he agreed that doing nothing would be malpractice. He then added: “I just think that would be a giant mistake having Luka in his prime.”Luka Doncic is posting the best numbers of his career, and the West is banged up. Anthony Edwards, Chet Holmgren and Cason Wallace are all hurt, which weakens three possible rivals. Slovenian guard is averaging 38.3 points, eight rebounds and 8.1 assists through seven games, shooting 49.7%. Hold that scoring pace all year and it would rank fourth on the NBA’s single-season list. Doncic has already set a handful of franchise and league records, and it has only been two weeks.Buha calls it a window Los Angeles has to use.When could a Lakers trade happen?Probably not soon. Many players who signed this summer cannot be moved until Dec. 15, so Buha sees the last week of December as the earliest realistic point. His best guess is closer to the Feb. 11 deadline.An injury or a bench unit that keeps struggling could speed things up, mostly at center. Walker Kessler is the only true big man on the roster, and nobody reliable sits behind him. The team has also been looking for a starting forward better than the wings it is using now. Buha was careful to say he is not promising anything. He just thinks a deal is more likely than not.There is a contract angle as well. Doncic’s deal runs through 2028 or 2029, depending on his player option. ESPN’s Brian Windhorst said before the season that the Lakers know they need to be in good standing with their star to get an extension done. Giving him a better supporting cast is part of that.Dec. 15 is the date to circle.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: ‘I Need to Do Better,’ ‘Maybe I Should Chill’ — Caitlin Clark Makes Honest Admission About Major Source of Criticism
articles.summary: Caitlin Clark has never been shy about showing emotion on the court, but the Indiana Fever star says one part of her competitive reputation may be overstated...
articles.body:
Caitlin Clark has never been shy about showing emotion on the court, but the Indiana Fever star says one part of her competitive reputation may be overstated.

During Tuesday's special episode of Kylie Kelce's "Not Gonna Lie" podcast, she was asked about her on-court behavior, leading to a candid admission about one tendency she knows she needs to work on.

Caitlin Clark Admits Referees Get More of Her Attention Than Opponents

Kelce asked whether the former No. 1 pick was an underrated trash talker, and she disagreed .

"See, people always think that I'm a trash talker. I don't even think I really am," Clark said.

She explained that her exchanges with opponents are usually playful, recalling a moment against Breanna Stewart and the New York Liberty during the 2025 season:

"There was a clip that went viral last year when we played the Liberty and I made a 3 over Stewie. And me and Stewie just both started laughing, 'cause it was funny."

The Fever guard then brought up another part of her on-court behavior:

"I don't really trash talk like that, honestly. I mean, if somebody says something to me, I'll probably go back. Honestly, the people I talk to the most is the refs, which I need to do better at. Maybe I should chill on that a little bit."

Kelce later asked if any particular player stood out as a trash talker. She said opponents rarely direct much trash talk her way.

"People don't really talk trash to me," Clark said, drawing a "What a flex" from Kelce.

The 2024 WNBA Rookie of the Year added that she enjoys those exchanges when they happen.

"I want you to say something to me," Clark said. "And I try to honestly do my best to just act like I can't hear. I love that. I think that's funny."

Her interactions with officials drew attention throughout the 2026 season, including an August technical foul that nearly resulted in a suspension.

During Indiana's 90-86 win over the Chicago Sky on Aug. 8, Natasha Cloud bumped Clark as she drove along the baseline. The Fever floor general passed the ball and went out of bounds, where her momentum carried her into an official.

The contact initially resulted in her eighth technical foul of the season. Fever coach Stephanie White also received one for arguing the call.

Indiana appealed immediately, and the WNBA rescinded the technical, ESPN's Kareem Copeland reported. The decision spared Clark a suspension that would have kept her out of the Fever's Aug. 11 home game against the Liberty.

It was the first time that season the Fever had successfully appealed a technical foul assessed to Clark. Even with the eighth rescinded, her seven technicals were tied for the most in the WNBA at that point.

The three-time All-Star picked up her second technical foul of the playoffs in her final game on Oct. 1. She and Las Vegas Aces forward Brianna Turner were assessed double technical fouls in the first quarter of Game 3 en route to Indiana's season-ending 94-83 road loss.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark’s latest heartwarming gesture sees her send a massive gift to her alma mater
articles.summary: Indiana Fever superstar Caitlin Clark had her former college team, the Iowa Hawkeyes, in mind after the Nike CC1 release. Clark dominated the NCAA with a fou...
articles.body:
Indiana Fever superstar Caitlin Clark had her former college team, the Iowa Hawkeyes, in mind after the Nike CC1 release.

Clark dominated the NCAA with a four-year stint with the Hawkeyes. Although she never won a national championship, losing in the 2023 and 2024 finals, she set countless records for the college and the NCAA as a whole.

Now with her third WNBA season in the rearview, Clark showed love to where she became a national superstar by sending a gift over to the current women's basketball team on the Hawkeyes.

Caitlin Clark gifts CC1s to Iowa Hawkeyes women's basketball team

Clark sent over custom black-and-gold Nike Caitlin 1 signature shoes to the Hawkeyes, creating a player-exclusive Iowa PE colorway for their season-opener against Towson. The team shared a video of the excited reactions current players had to the gift.

The Hawkeyes also shared an in-game picture of how the sneakers looked on the players' feet during the game.

While Clark has previously gifted sneakers to the Hawkeyes team, including pairs of the CC1s, this is the first time she has created a team-exclusive PE for the players, featuring the University of Iowa Tigerhawk logo on the tongue.

The Hawkeyes picked up a convincing 73-45 win over the Towson Tigers in their CBB season-opener on November 3. Junior Dani Carnegie, who was a freshman during Clark's final year with the Hawkeyes, led them to the win with 21 points, five rebounds and five assists.

Clark left the Hawkeyes without a championship, but set the NCAA Division 1 basketball scoring record with 2,951 points, breaking Pete Maravich's 54-year-old 3,667-point record.

She has also made the most three-pointers in NCAA history with 548, with her 201 threes in 23-24 setting the record for most in one season.

Her legacy as a Hawkeye is arguably richer than any current professional athlete due to the historic nature of her four-year tenure. While not having a championship to cement it as the greatest NCAA career of all time is rough, she gave Iowa years of incredible basketball.

articles.title: ‘This Would Literally Ruin Basketball,’ ‘Do Not Do That’ — NBA World Outraged As Adam Silver ‘Likes the Idea’ Of 40-Minute Games
articles.summary: NBA fans are pushing back against the possibility of shorter games after a recent report suggested Adam Silver prefers reducing NBA contests from 48 to 40 mi...
articles.body:
NBA fans are pushing back against the possibility of shorter games after a recent report suggested Adam Silver prefers reducing NBA contests from 48 to 40 minutes.

Sports Illustrated's Chris Mannix recently discussed the commissioner's preference, but the idea is not new, and Silver has openly supported it before.

NBA Fans Outraged as Adam Silver's 40-Minute Game Preference Resurfaces

Mannix discussed the possibility during a recent appearance alongside Rachel Nichols on Sports Illustrated. He said Silver likes the idea of replacing the NBA's traditional four 12-minute quarters with four 10-minute periods, bringing games in line with the international format.

"Adam Silver likes the idea of 40-minute games. Adam's a globalist when it comes to basketball. But I just don't see financially how it is feasible," Mannix said .

He also explained that shortening games would not necessarily reduce the workload of the biggest stars. Instead, he believes players further down the rotation would lose opportunities.

The comments quickly drew criticism from basketball fans, many of whom believe changing the length of NBA games would affect the sport's identity and history.

"This would literally ruin basketball," one hoops fan wrote .

A Pacers fan account also warned about the impact on historical comparisons, saying : "NO… this would change basketball history and how we compare stats across generations."

Others directed their frustration at the commissioner, as one user wrote : "Adam Silver needs to be fired IMMEDIATELY."

"This dude sucks at his job," a sports content creator quipped.

However, the first time Silver publicly expressed the idea was in January 2025. He appeared on The Dan Patrick Show and openly said he was a fan of four 10-minute quarters.

"As we get more involved in global basketball, the NBA is the only league that plays 48 minutes," Silver explained . "I am a fan of four 10-minute quarters."

Silver argued that a two-hour game would better fit modern television viewing habits, citing Olympic and college basketball, both of which use a 40-minute format. He also acknowledged that shortening games could affect records and statistics, although he said he was putting those concerns aside when discussing the idea.

At the time, ESPN reported that NBA games averaged 2 hours and 16 minutes, making them considerably longer than the two-hour format Silver preferred. The discussion also drew opposition from coaches.

A switch would have significant consequences beyond the length of games. NBA games have featured four 12-minute quarters throughout the league's history, and reducing them to 10 minutes would make many scoring and playing-time records harder to compare across generations.

While Mannix's latest comments have revived an old debate, they do not mean the league is preparing to introduce 40-minute games.
